title: Interface and Event Contract Format
context: The standards profile classifies OpenAPI-style interface contracts and AsyncAPI-style event contracts as adapted principles with artefact adoption deferred. Draft USF interface-contract and event-contract schemas already exist.
decision: USF-native JSON contract artefacts are canonical for this phase. Interface contracts are shaped by interface-contract.schema.json and event contracts are shaped by event-contract.schema.json. OpenAPI and AsyncAPI remain adapted principles only unless a later ADR and validator changes adopt or generate reconciled projections.
consequences: Interface and event contract work can proceed using the existing schemas.
External-standard compliance claims remain honest and limited.
Future drift checks must target USF-native contract artefacts first.
invariants: Contract instances must validate against the USF-native schemas for this phase.
OpenAPI and AsyncAPI principles may inform structure but do not define USF contract authority.
Future OpenAPI or AsyncAPI projections must reconcile back to the USF-native contract artefacts.
permittedChanges: Add drift checks that compare runtime routes or emitted events to USF-native contracts.
Add generated OpenAPI or AsyncAPI projections if they are explicitly non-authoritative and validator-reconciled.
Adopt OpenAPI or AsyncAPI as an authoritative artefact form through a later ADR.
forbiddenDrift: Do not claim OpenAPI compliance without concrete OpenAPI artefacts and validators.
Do not claim AsyncAPI compliance without concrete AsyncAPI artefacts and validators.
Do not infer contracts from handlers or emitters when semantic contracts exist.
Do not let generated projections override USF-native contracts.
aiAlignmentRules: Agents must read USF-native contracts before reasoning from source code.
Agents must avoid false compliance language.
Agents must surface any conflict between generated projections and USF-native contracts.
rationale: The draft USF schemas encode governance envelope, controlled vocabulary bindings, source references, and fail-closed contract fields needed now, while direct OpenAPI or AsyncAPI adoption would risk false compliance claims before reconciliation.
description: Records the contract-format decision for interface and event contracts.
aiGuidance: Use USF-native contract schemas as the contract authority for this phase and avoid OpenAPI or AsyncAPI compliance claims.
